The '''2011–12 [[La Liga]]''' season (known as the ''Liga BBVA'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 81st season of the top level Spanish association football competition. The campaign began on 27 August 2011, and concluded on 13 May 2012. [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] won a record 32nd title following victory over [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 2 May 2012. 

Real Madrid broke a number of league records, including most points in a single season (100), most goals scored (121), best goal difference (+89), most away wins (16), and most overall wins (32). This season also saw [[Lionel Messi]] score a record 50 league goals in 37 games. Behind Messi was Real Madrid's [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], who scored 46 goals; the pair's combined tally of 96 goals was the most ever by two players playing in the same major European league in the same season.

==Teams==
[[Deportivo de La Coruña]], [[Hércules CF]] from [[Alicante]] and [[UD Almería]] were relegated to the [[2011–12 Segunda División]] after finishing in the bottom three spots of the table at the end of the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 season]]. Deportivo were relegated to the Segunda División after 20 seasons of continuous membership in the top football league of Spain, while Almería ended a four-year tenure in La Liga and Hércules made their immediate return to the second level.

The three relegated teams were replaced by three [[2010–11 Segunda División]] sides. Champions [[Real Betis|Betis]], who terminated their second-level status after two years, runners-up [[Rayo Vallecano]], who returned to the top flight after eight seasons at lower levels, earned direct promotion.

The third promoted team was decided in the [[2011 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]] where [[Granada CF]] returned to the league for the first time in 35 years, having spent 26 of them in [[Segunda División B]] and [[Tercera División]].

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] is awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.

===Fair Play award===
This award was given annually since 1999 to the team with the best fair play during the season. This ranking takes into account [[La Liga#Competition format|aspects]]<ref name="Liga fair play rules">{{cite news|title=Criterios de puntuación del juego limpio |trans-title=Fair Play score criteria |url=http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298#ancla2 |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF]] |date=30 October 1998 |access-date=18 May 2010 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407195555/http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298 |archive-date=7 April 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> such as cards, suspension of matches, audience behaviour and other penalties. This section not only aims to determine the best fair play, but also serves to break the tie in teams that are tied in all the other rules: points, head-to-head, goal difference and goals scored.
